items.t: Enel stock gets new grid signal from Colombia infrastructure plan
sum: Enel is adding a new grid-infrastructure angle to its investment case after a regional plan in Colombia outlined more than 30 electricity projects. The initiative expands the focus beyond the Chile battery pipeline discussed in the previous report.

The Bogotá-Región 2030 plan covers substations, high-voltage lines and medium-voltage networks across Bogotá and Cundinamarca. According to La Republica, 14 projects are already operating, two are under construction and the remaining initiatives are moving through studies and environmental licensing.

The operating projects have lifted installed capacity in Bogotá and Cundinamarca from 3,510 MVA to 4,860 MVA, according to the same report. Projects under construction include the Intexzona and Guaymaral substations, which are planned to add 246 MVA to the regional transmission system.

The plan offers visibility on network investment and regional power demand, but projects still in studies or licensing have a longer route to operation. The report does not provide a direct earnings contribution for the individual projects, so the near-term financial impact remains tied to execution and the group's broader results.

Enel stock traded at 9.68 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:47 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026, 0.10 percent below the Xetra close of 9.69 euros on Friday, November 6. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Enel stock.
The broader FTSE MIB market provides the relevant Italian equity backdrop for Enel stock.

Enel stock gains as Chile battery pipeline reaches 600 MW
sum: Enel stock traded at 9.48 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:31 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 1.72 percent above the Xetra close of Tuesday, November 3. The move comes as Enel's Chilean subsidiary advances four battery energy storage systems with a combined capacity of 600 megawatts.

Argus Media reported on October 29 that construction remains on track, citing Enel Chile chief executive Gianluca Palumbo during a results conference call. The projects will operate alongside existing solar and wind plants and use grid-forming technology, which helps maintain voltage and frequency as renewable generation takes a larger role in the power system.

The first project to begin operations is the 205-megawatt Las Salinas battery. It has recently connected to the grid and is expected to start commercial operations in 2027. The project would be Chile's first battery installation using grid-forming technology, according to Argus Media.

The 153-megawatt Valle del Sol and 94-megawatt Azabache projects are also scheduled to start in 2027. Construction of the 100-megawatt Finis Terrae project began in August, with commissioning planned for 2028. Once all four facilities are complete, Enel Chile's battery storage capacity in the country is expected to reach 800 megawatts.

For Enel, the projects extend the strategic role of storage beyond adding generation capacity. Grid-forming batteries can provide system support traditionally associated with conventional power plants, potentially helping renewable assets operate in a more stable network. The projects also give the group a visible pipeline in a market where regulation is encouraging the integration of grid-forming capability into battery, solar and wind facilities.

The storage update was accompanied by stronger operating figures at Enel Chile. January-to-September profit rose 11 percent year on year to 390 million US dollars, while hydro generation increased 3 percent to 8.2 terawatt-hours after heavier rainfall from August. Enel Chile is the country's largest generator, with installed capacity of 8.9 gigawatts.
The earnings improvement does not remove the wider risks for the group.

Enel stock faces results test as Endesa regulated earnings gain weight
sum: Enel stock faces its next earnings test after subsidiary Endesa reported stronger nine-month results on October 28. The update adds a more detailed read-through on earnings quality before Enel presents its group figures on November 12.

Endesa's official results release said net profit rose 15 percent to EUR 1.962 billion and ordinary net profit increased 22 percent to EUR 2.125 billion. EBITDA advanced 8.4 percent to EUR 4.577 billion, allowing the subsidiary to confirm its target of more than EUR 2.4 billion in ordinary net profit for 2026.

Regulated businesses, led by electricity distribution and generation in non-peninsular territories, now contribute nearly half of Endesa's EBITDA, compared with approximately 40 percent a year earlier. Distribution EBITDA rose 24.8 percent to EUR 1.747 billion, supported by the regulatory framework introduced in January and settlements from previous fiscal years.

The mix also carries a caution for Enel investors. Combined EBITDA from generation and commercialisation grew 3 percent to EUR 2.889 billion, but higher renewable generation did not prevent a lower renewables gross margin because realised power prices fell and solar curtailment increased.

Gross investment increased 19.4 percent to EUR 1.622 billion, including about EUR 900 million for distribution networks, up 42 percent year on year. Electricity distributed rose to 114 terawatt-hours from 109 terawatt-hours, while grid losses improved from 9.5 percent to 9 percent. Endesa generated EUR 3.5 billion of cash flow and ended the period with EUR 11.187 billion of net financial debt.

Enel stock traded at 9.26 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 14:21 CET on Monday, November 2, 2026, 0.54 percent below the Xetra close of Friday, October 30, at 9.31 euros. The real-time quote of Enel stock provides the latest trading indication.
Italian equities remain influenced by the broader FTSE MIB market alongside company-specific earnings expectations.
